newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus cuts quota for compulsory currency swap.
newsitem.headline: Belarus cuts quota for compulsory currency swap.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko issued a decree on Wednesday easing the amount of export revenues companies must change on the Minsk Interbank Currency Exchange (MICE) to 30 percent from 50 percent.
The decree gave firms five days to change currencies, including Russian roubles, following completion of transactions.
Banks failing to comply with the order will be deducted one percent of the earnings for each day the deadline is missed.
Joint ventures holding more than 30 percent foreign investment were exempt from the decree. Those with less than 30 percent were exempt if they registered before it was passed.
Also exempt were banks accounts holding starting capital, and money used for business operations and purchase of bonds.
The World Bank has said it may be ready to renew credits of $100 million a year to the former Soviet republic if it liberalises its financial markets.
